subject: Contoso: request for audit-log retention exception & subprocessor confirmation
messages:
From: Ellen Smythe <ellen.smythe@contosohealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@contosohealth.com; procurement@contosohealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: audit-log retention exception & subprocessor confirmation for pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday — Contoso Health is excited to move the pilot to production. A few legal/procurement asks came up while reviewing the DPA:

- We need an extension for audit/log retention tied to the pilot: 12 months of immutable audit logs (standard DPA shows 90 days). This is for regulatory audit readiness.
- Please confirm all subprocessors who will touch unredacted logs for the pilot. DataStream Analytics is listed in your vendor matrix; we need confirmation of their role and whether they receive persistent copies.
- We prefer a carveout that explicitly prevents any model training or derivative model use on customer logs (Contoso-sourced inference telemetry).

I've attached a redlined DPA and a short proposed clause for the audit-log retention. Can you route to your Product & Security teams for sign-off? Tim Jones at DataStream is copied for visibility.

Attachments: contoso_dpa_redline_v3.pdf

Best,
Ellen Smythe
Counsel, Contoso Health
ellen.smythe@contosohealth.com

Folks — forwarding Contoso's redline (attached). Key asks: 12m immutable audit logs, confirmation about DataStream Analytics access, and explicit prohibition on training on Contoso logs. Contoso says pilot goes live mid-April and wants this in the signed DPA.

Quick context: this is a mid-sized pilot (CN-4721) with potential expansion to enterprise in Q3. Procurement is pushing for the DPA to be agreed before the pilot kicks off.

Can Product weigh in on operational impact (storage/retention architecture) and Security on acceptability of the subprocessor behavior and the training carveout? Legal has been CCed for redline routing. I'll propose a 48-hour turnaround to Contoso if possible.

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: audit-log retention exception & subprocessor confirmation for pilot

Thanks for the ping, Mateo. High-level Security feedback below. I added numbered asks to make it action-oriented for Contoso.

1) Training carveout: strong +1. We need explicit language: "Customer Data, including audit logs and telemetry, will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any models (including third-party models) without Customer's prior written consent." That must be in the DPA.

2) Subprocessor access: we need a precise statement of DataStream's scope. If they process unredacted logs, we require:
   - Data minimization: only the minimum fields required for analytics.
   - No persistent storage of full unredacted logs unless encrypted and access-controlled for <90 days unless an exception approved by Security.
   - Logging and proof of deletion (s3 lifecycle + deletion receipts) for any retained copies.

3) Immutable audit logs for 12 months: operationally feasible but increases storage and egress cost. If we accept, Product must provide an export path for Contoso (read-only S3 bucket with MFA delete or signed time-limited exports) so we don't expand our long-term retention footprint unnecessarily.

4) Telemetry: we need to confirm that telemetry events linked to Contoso customer IDs will be pseudonymized by default and stored separate from raw logs. If Contoso requires raw telemetry retention, that needs additional approvals and an incident response plan.

Please send me a proposed clause that captures the above. Legal (Ben) — please review wording for liability/indemnity interaction. Aditya — estimate cost delta for 12m immutable retention + S3 export in the pilot region (us-west-2).

- Olga
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: audit-log retention exception & subprocessor confirmation for pilot

Thanks — can confirm Product's take after quick triage:

- 12mo immutable audit logs: feasible for a bounded pilot if Contoso pays a retention premium. Operational approach: write-once audit bucket (us-west-2) with lifecycle rules and a read-only export bucket for Contoso with cross-account access. Requires: storage budget line in pilot SOW and S3 MFA-delete for true immutability.

- DataStream Analytics: per our current contracts, DataStream can run analytics in a transient compute environment; they do not typically keep persistent full-log copies. We will require DataStream to sign a subprocessor addendum for this pilot that enforces deletion receipts and prohibits model training on Contoso data. We can get them to agree to a <90-day retention by default and produce deletion proof.

- Training prohibition: Product supports the explicit DPA language Olga suggested. No-objection on Product side.

Proposed language (short):
"Customer Data and Customer Audit Logs will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models or derivatives, including by third-party subprocessors, without the Customer's prior written consent. Subprocessors that process Customer Audit Logs for analytics shall not retain full-log copies longer than ninety (90) days, except where Customer expressly authorizes longer retention by written agreement. Provider will provide record-level deletion receipts for any retained copies and will provide a read-only export mechanism for Customer within thirty (30) days of request."

Next steps:
- Legal to review the short clause and confirm liability language (Ben).
- Aditya to provide an estimate for incremental cost & a one-time configuration plan for cross-account export.

If everyone is ok, we can push a redlined clause back to Contoso tomorrow morning.

- Marissa
VP, Product — Inference Platform
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ellen Smythe <ellen.smythe@contosohealth.com>
Cc: Tim Jones <tim.jones@datastream-analytics.com>, contracts@contosohealth.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: audit-log retention exception & subprocessor confirmation for pilot

Ellen — thanks for the redline and patience. Quick update and proposed next steps from Redwood:

1) Training carveout: Redwood can accept explicit, mutual language preventing the use of Contoso's logs for model training without prior written consent. See the redlined clause attached (proposed_auditlog_clause_20280322.docx).

2) DataStream Analytics: Tim (copied) — DataStream will need to sign our standard subprocessor addendum for the pilot that includes deletion receipts and a 90-day default retention; Contoso can request a documented exception for 12m but that requires an additional SOW line item.

3) 12-month immutable audit logs: Product and Security require a storage/egress premium for a 12m immutable window. Proposal: Contoso covers the incremental retention cost for the pilot and we provide a read-only cross-account S3 export (MFA-delete enabled) with signed access logs. This keeps our internal long-term footprint constrained.

4) Action plan / timeline:
   - Today: Redwood legal to review & finalize redlined clause (Ben).
   - Mon 2028-03-26: DataStream to sign subprocessor addendum; Aditya will share cost delta and S3 config details.
   - Tue 2028-03-27: Redwood sends final DPA + pilot SOW with a retention line.
   - Contoso: sign DocuSign envelope (link included)

Attached: proposed_auditlog_clause_20280322.docx (redline). DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/containers/Envelope-ABC123

Can you confirm Contoso's willingness to cover the incremental retention cost for the pilot and confirm Tim's sign-off timeline? If yes, we'll aim to have the DPA wrapped next week.

Best,
Mateo
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Attachments: proposed_auditlog_clause_20280322.docx
